title: REV-ERBalpha Inhibits Osteoclastogenesis and Protects against Alveolar Bone Loss.
authors: Zhang, C; Tan, L; Li, J; Shen, Z; Yao, J; Huang, Y; Wu, L; Yu, C; Gao, L; Zhao, C
one_liner_zh: 该文研究REV-ERBalpha在牙周炎骨吸收中的作用，聚焦昼夜节律与破骨细胞分化，未涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、转录因子结合机制或AI/物理模拟建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Circadian rhythm disruption is thought to be associated with periodontitis, and molecular clock genes play critical roles in regulating bone homeostasis. However, the specific contribution of molecular clock genes to alveolar bone resorption caused by periodontitis is poorly understood. In this study, we introduced a novel Periodontitis Circadian Rhythm Score (PeriCRS) model that was established through machine learning using periodontal transcriptomic data from periodontitis clinical cohorts in the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. This approach revealed the potential regulatory role of circadian rhythm disruption in periodontitis and identified key molecular clock genes associated with alveolar bone destruction. Moreover, we established an experimental periodontitis model with circadian rhythm disturbance via periodontal ligation in mice exposed to a 6-h advanced LD12:12 cycle every 2 d. Our bioinformatics analysis revealed that NR1D1, which encodes REV-ERBalpha, is a pivotal factor in the impact of circadian rhythm disruption on periodontitis in periodontal tissues. Next, we confirmed the abnormal expression of the molecular clock gene Rev-erbalpha in inflammatory periodontal tissue in mice and confirmed that circadian rhythm disruption altered REV-ERBalpha expression. Furthermore, the activation of REV-ERBalpha with the agonist SR9009 notably decreased RANKL-induced osteoclast differentiation and suppressed the expression of osteoclast-related factors. Subsequent in vivo experiments demonstrated that SR9009 mitigated alveolar bone loss caused by periodontitis. Mechanistically, we found that the IL-22-STAT3 pathway inhibited REV-ERBalpha expression and modulated RANKL-induced osteoclast differentiation in vitro. Our results elucidate the role of REV-ERBalpha in osteoclastogenesis and suggest a potential new therapeutic avenue for addressing alveolar bone resorption associated with periodontitis.
abstract_zh: 昼夜节律紊乱被认为与牙周炎相关，分子时钟基因在调节骨稳态中发挥关键作用。然而，分子时钟基因对牙周炎引起的牙槽骨吸收的具体贡献尚不清楚。在本研究中，我们引入了一种新型的牙周炎昼夜节律评分（Periodontitis Circadian Rhythm Score, PeriCRS）模型，该模型通过使用基因表达综合数据库（Gene Expression Omnibus, GEO）中牙周炎临床队列的牙周转录组数据进行机器学习而建立。该方法揭示了昼夜节律紊乱在牙周炎中的潜在调控作用，并识别了与牙槽骨破坏相关的关键分子时钟基因。此外，我们通过将小鼠暴露于每2天一次6小时提前的LD12:12循环中，并采用牙周结扎方法，建立了伴有昼夜节律紊乱的实验性牙周炎模型。我们的生物信息学分析揭示，编码REV-ERBalpha的NR1D1是昼夜节律紊乱影响牙周组织中牙周炎的关键因素。接下来，我们确认了小鼠炎症性牙周组织中分子时钟基因Rev-erbalpha的异常表达，并证实昼夜节律紊乱改变了REV-ERBalpha的表达。此外，使用激动剂SR9009激活REV-ERBalpha显著减少了RANKL诱导的破骨细胞分化，并抑制了破骨细胞相关因子的表达。随后的体内实验表明，SR9009减轻了牙周炎引起的牙槽骨丢失。在机制上，我们发现IL-22-STAT3通路在体外抑制REV-ERBalpha表达并调节RANKL诱导的破骨细胞分化。我们的结果阐明了REV-ERBalpha在破骨细胞生成中的作用，并为解决与牙周炎相关的牙槽骨吸收提出了潜在的新治疗途径。
